To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of decision tree based predictive models for breast cancer survivability is affected by the data distribution.

(1) the performance of the model for 5-year breast cancer survivability prediction is best when the distribution of data are approximately equal, and (2) the performance of integration decision tree is the best among all the models for 5 year breast cancer survivability on imbalanced data.
(a) the performance of models is better while the distribution of the data is approximately equal; (b) the performance of integration decision tree model is better than the single model.
